free_tier.stated: 2 GB file storage on the Free plan (10 users, unlimited spaces and pages). Crucially: 'Free, Standard, and Premium plans entitle you to one app instance. **You can have as many of these plans as you need.** You'll subscribe to each one separately.' Each instance 'will have its own storage'.

retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: No egress meter anywhere in Atlassian Cloud pricing. Attachments are served from the site domain, not a billed CDN bucket.

tooling: Confluence Cloud REST API v2/v1 (`/wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/child/attachment`), Basic auth with email + API token, or OAuth 2.0. No rclone backend; the API is the client.
chaining: 2 GB x N free Confluence sites, and N is self-service and explicitly unbounded ('as many of these plans as you need'). Ten free sites = 20 GB; a scripted site-creation loop is the multiplier. Community reports confirm multiple free sites per account are allowed and the one-instance limit is a *paid*-plan construct.
limits_note: per-object-cap: attachment default 100 MB, admin-configurable upward ('Enter your preferred maximum size (in bytes)'). Quota is per-site, not per-org. request-rate: Atlassian Cloud REST rate limits apply. Retention: Free sites are DEACTIVATED after a period of inactivity (logging in and viewing a page counts as activity) — this is the real hazard, not eviction. Over-quota does not delete data, it restricts editing/creating.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Nothing is deleted at quota — writes are blocked until you upgrade or free space. But a Free site that goes untouched is deactivated, so a storage-only site needs a periodic login to stay alive.
